name: Berkshire Museum
source: Berkshire Museum: reopening news (2026); its Google Arts & Culture pages; Wikimedia Commons
note: The Berkshire Museum has no open online collection, and its website asks AI tools not to read it, so this list is built from news of the 2026 reopening, the architects’ description of the new galleries and the museum’s own Google Arts & Culture pages. The galleries and the Brooklyn Museum show are on view now. The art at the end belongs to the museum but may not be on view (the Cabinets of Curiosities and Objects and Their Stories rotate).

works.title: Indian Prince, Palace of Agra
works.description: This oriental genre scene captures a group entering through a red stone arch and assembling in a courtyard of the Palace of Agra. The prince rides a pure white horse and is flanked by his two attendants on foot. Behind this group another Indian, flanked by attendants, enters through the archway. Already in the courtyard, an armored warrior astride his mount, faces (away from the viewer) a group of nabob observers who watch the proceedings from a white verandah above the gallery on the side of the arch.

works.title: Study of Thomas Carlyle
works.description: This drawing is a preliminary study for one of the Whistler's best known paintings entitled Arrangement in Grey and Black, No.2: Portrait of Thomas Carlyle, which is now in the collection of the City Art Gallery in Glasgow, Scotland. Several other studies for this masterpiece exist, notable a pastel version in the Freer Gallery, a pen drawing in the Fogg Art Museum, and oil sketch in the Art Institute of Chicago, and the present example.

works.title: Henrik Hudson entering New York Harbor, September 11, 1609
works.description: The oil painting shows a ship in the distance on a still sea under a cloudy sky, sailing toward an Indian looking up over a rock on the shore in the foreground. The location of the painting is at the south end of Staten Island looking across Raritan Bay towards Sandy Hook, which Hudson's log book noted as the area of his first exploration. Description from Theodore Sutro, 1905: "The interest of this painting centers in the scene, which it vividly depicts, of the effect upon the natives of this first sight of a ship. Nothing could be more intense than the expression of mignled fear and defiant surprise portrayed in the face and attitude of the young Indian warrior, that so strange an object should dare to approach his hitherto undisputed domain of the shore." (This refers to a slightly different copy of the painting from 1898.)

works.title: Still Life with Fruit
works.description: Fruits in a symmetrical arrangement in the center of a table on a white cloth. The combination of two pears, a round fruit, and a banana at the center of the combination look like a smiling face. Description from appraisal: "Citing the ordinary, rather than grandiose, this work of art shows an arrangement of fruit around a glass vase holding flowers, centered on a round white cloth which is draped over a red covered table. The colors are bold, and highlight the identity of each piece of fruit in their environment. The table and background are painted in strong colors, and with much gesture or movement. This dynamic aspect coupled with the sensitivity of line and hint of shadow are inspired by the spirituality for which Hartley's work is known. The focus of the subject is the center point of the picture, and the perspective in the whole piece is foreshortened, thus bringing the artist's expression closer for greater impact on the viewer."

works.title: Fon sword
works.description: Fon swords of Benin, formally Dahomey. The handle is five and a half inches long. The pommel is a large metal ball. The grip is four inches long, and plain with the exception of a golden streak down both sides of the grip. The blade is twenty and three quarters of an inch long. The blade forms the shape of a closed hand with the thumb erect and the index finger pointing forwards. The hand's finger nails have been painted gold, and the lines bettween fingers have been painted a bronze color. There is a plate, seperate from the blade, and yet attached in the shape of a small lizard. It has a slender body, four feet, each with two toes, and a tail that curls up behind it. The head is a large circle, and its teeth have been cut into its open mouth. Its eyes have been attached in the form of small gold colored caps, with a bronze dot on the top. The lizard is decorated with small wavy lines on its feet, tail, and near its mouth, while the rest of its body is covered in diamonds with little circles inside.
